title: Recording architectural decisions (ADRs) and defending them

videos.script: Every lesson in this course ended with a choice and the reasons for it. Synchronous or asynchronous. Consistent or available. One database or several. {{choices}} In a real team those reasons live in somebody's head, a meeting nobody recorded, a chat thread that scrolled away. A year later the choice is still in the code, and the reasons are gone. {{gone}} An architecture decision record is the habit of writing the reasons down, one short file per decision, kept with the code. {{adr}} On your machine you will write Quitanda's log: the decisions this course made, in the format Michael Nygard proposed. {{log}} Then a decision changes, the way the stock decision did between lessons 5 and 9, and you will see how a record is replaced without being rewritten. {{supersede}} And you will defend one decision the strongest way there is, with a check that fails the build when the code goes against it. {{defend}} Writing the reasons down is what turns an architecture into something a team can argue with, and change on purpose.
